chmmc-2013-tiebreaker-01.title: Power of a point and the law of cosines
chmmc-2013-tiebreaker-01.body:
By the tangent-secant theorem $BA^2=BD\cdot BC$, so $BC=\frac{36}{3}=12$. The arc $AC$ is $\frac{2\pi}3$, so $\angle AOC=120^\circ$ and $\angle OAC=\angle OCA=30^\circ$. The tangent is perpendicular to $OA$, so $\angle BAC=90^\circ+30^\circ=120^\circ$ (as in the figure, $B$ lies on the far side of $A$ from $C$).

Law of cosines in $\triangle ABC$: $144=36+AC^2+6\,AC$, i.e. $AC^2+6AC-108=0$, so $AC=-3+3\sqrt{13}$.

In the isosceles triangle $OAC$ with apex angle $120^\circ$, $AC=2R\sin60^\circ=R\sqrt3$. Hence $$R=\frac{3\sqrt{13}-3}{\sqrt3}=\sqrt{39}-\sqrt3\approx4.51.$$

**Answer: $\sqrt{39}-\sqrt3$**

chmmc-2013-tiebreaker-01.title: Coordinates
chmmc-2013-tiebreaker-01.body:
Put $O=(0,0)$, $A=(R,0)$, so the tangent at $A$ is the line $x=R$ and $B=(R,-6)$ (the side shown in the figure). Then $C=(R\cos120^\circ,R\sin120^\circ)=(-\tfrac R2,\tfrac{\sqrt3}2R)$ and $BC^2=\left(\tfrac{3R}2\right)^2+\left(6+\tfrac{\sqrt3}2R\right)^2=R^2\cdot3+6\sqrt3R+36$. Power of a point gives $BC=12$, so $3R^2+6\sqrt3R+36=144$, $R^2+2\sqrt3R-36=0$, and $R=-\sqrt3+\sqrt{39}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{39}-\sqrt3$**

chmmc-2013-tiebreaker-02.title: Vieta's formulas
chmmc-2013-tiebreaker-02.body:
The equation is $x^4-3x^2+6x-13=0$. The sum of the roots is $0$ (no $x^3$ term), so $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=-\delta$ and so on. The expression becomes $$-\left(\frac1\alpha+\frac1\beta+\frac1\gamma+\frac1\delta\right)=-\frac{e_3}{e_4},$$ where $e_3=-6$ and $e_4=-13$ (from $x^4-e_1x^3+e_2x^2-e_3x+e_4$). So the value is $-\frac{-6}{-13}=-\frac6{13}$.

(The official key, $-\frac12$, corresponds to ignoring the $+1$ on the right and using $e_4=-12$.)

**Answer: $-\dfrac{6}{13}$**

chmmc-2013-tiebreaker-03.title: Complement
chmmc-2013-tiebreaker-03.body:
The winning rolls are $(1,3),(3,1),(2,6),(6,2)$: $4$ of $36$, probability $\frac19$. The probability of never winning in three games is $\left(\frac89\right)^3=\frac{512}{729}$, so the probability of winning at least once is $1-\frac{512}{729}=\frac{217}{729}$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{217}{729}$**

chmmc-2013-tiebreaker-04.title: Expand a product
chmmc-2013-tiebreaker-04.body:
$A,B,C$ are the elementary symmetric sums $e_1,e_2,e_3$ of $\frac12,\frac13,\frac15,\frac19$, and $e_4=\frac1{2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot9}=\frac1{270}$. Then $$1+e_1+e_2+e_3+e_4=\left(1+\tfrac12\right)\left(1+\tfrac13\right)\left(1+\tfrac15\right)\left(1+\tfrac19\right)=\tfrac32\cdot\tfrac43\cdot\tfrac65\cdot\tfrac{10}9=\tfrac83.$$ So $A+B+C=\frac83-1-\frac1{270}=\frac{720-270-1}{270}=\frac{449}{270}$.

**Answer: $\dfrac{449}{270}$**
